item.title: PFF Grades Reveal Detroit Lions’ Biggest Standouts From Win Over Buccaneers
item.description: The Detroit Lions beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 31-21 on Sunday , and the Detroit Lions PFF grades include a linebacker who needed only 25 snaps to make the list. Detroit improved to 8-2 on the season with the win, while Tampa Bay dropped to 3-7. Here are the top three Lions on each side of the ball, according to PFF . Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff (16) tucks the ball and runs for the first down while being chased by Tampa Bay Buccaneers outside linebacker Al-Quadin Muhammad (97) during the second half of the NFL game at Ford Field in Detroit, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Chuck Clark led the defense in Detroit Lions PFF grades Safety Chuck Clark led Detroit’s defense on PFF with a grade of 85.7. He played 69 snaps in the game. Clark had eight combined tackles (two solo), one sack, one TFL, and one pass deflection. He had another solid game for the Lions on defense. Linebacker Malcolm Rodriguez was ranked second on the Lions defense on PFF for this matchup against Tampa Bay. He played 55 snaps and had an 83.5 grade on PFF . Rodriguez had six tackles, 0.5 sacks, and one pass deflection. Linebacker K.J. Britt was ranked fifth overall in the game, and he was Detroit’s third-best defensive player. He had a 75.1 PFF grade and played just 25 snaps. Britt had three tackles and one TFL in the game. Jared Goff led the Lions offense on PFF Quarterback Jared Goff had a strong day for the Lions. He completed 20 of 28 passes for 279 yards and two touchdowns without an interception. Goff had the highest grade on offense for the team on PFF . He played 58 snaps and had a grade of 88.3. Jahmyr Gibbs and Jameson Williams round out the top three Running back Jahmyr Gibbs was ranked second on PFF for the Lions on offense. He had an 82.7 grade and played 43 snaps. Gibbs rushed for 98 yards and two touchdowns on 23 carries. He also had four receptions for 20 yards. Gibbs continues to be a workhorse for the Lions on offense. Wide receiver Jameson Williams was the third-best Lions offensive player on PFF, but he was ranked fourth overall in the game. Williams played 45 snaps and had a 74.5 PFF grade . He caught four passes for 93 yards, an average of 23.3 yards per reception, including a 57-yard touchdown. The Bears are next on Thanksgiving This was another huge game for the offense and defense. The Lions will need this kind of performance again in a Thanksgiving showdown with first place on the line against the Chicago Bears, who are also 8-2.

item.title: TELEGRAPH: Williams-Barnett on the brink of a new Tottenham contract
item.description: LONDON, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 21: Luca Williams-Barnett of Tottenham Hotspur is the centre of attention as his colleagues celebrate his opening goal during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Tottenham Hotspur and Ipswich Town at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on November 21, 2026 in London, United Kingdom. (Photo by Mark Leech/Offside/Offside via Getty Images) | Offside via Getty Images Well, THAT didn’t take long! Two days after Luca Williams-Barnett introduced himself to the Premier League with a great flourish — scoring a goal and tallying an assist in his first ever Premier League start and leading Spurs to a 2-0 win over Ipswich Town — he’s on the verge of signing a lucrative new contract that will keep him at Tottenham Hotspur for the foreseeable future. According to Matt Law in the Telegraph , Williams-Barnett is very close to signing a new deal with Spurs that will lock down his future at the club. Williams-Barnett is one of the brightest young stars to come out of any Premier League academy in recent years, and the list of clubs that are interested in trying to buy him away from Spurs is long, but includes Chelsea and Borussia Dortmund. It’s also a very unique opportunity for Luca, who due to injuries to Savio, Wilson Odobert, and Mykhailo Mudryk, now has a claim to the starting left winger role at Spurs. Williams-Barnett is only 18 years old, but has made a significant splash in the league, probably as big a splash as any Tottenham academy grad since before Harry Kane. Interestingly, while left back appears to be his current position, Law cites people close to Spurs who suggest LWB could end up being an attacking midfield #10 in the future, and that’s likely his best position. The left wing position is crowded at Spurs (though injury certainly has opened a window for Luca), as is the #10 role, with James Maddison and Xavi Simons, as well as players like Mateus Fernandes, Omar Marmoush, and Conor Gallagher able to play there. But you can certainly make an argument that Maddison is unlikely to be around for too much longer as he ages, and LWB could easily rotate into the position alongside Simons and whoever else Spurs decide to bring in for the future. It’s an exciting time to be a Spurs fan, that’s for sure. Hopefully we’ll see Luca lining up for Tottenham for years to come.

item.title: ‘I’m the best in the world’: Giants star Abdul Carter sends a message to the NFL after dominant game
item.description: Nov 22, 2026; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; New York Giants linebacker Abdul Carter (3) on the field after the national anthem before the game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images New York Giants linebacker Abdul Carter came into Sunday’s game against the Jacksonville Jaguars facing plenty of questions about his lack of sacks this season. He spent the week promising that he would show the world what he could do, and then he went out and did exactly that. Carter recorded two sacks, hit Trevor Lawrence five times, and was credited with 12 pressures in the Giants’ 23-18 win. And after the game, the second-year star didn’t hold back, declaring that he is “the best in the world.” Abdul Carter’s Slow Start The Giants took Carter with the No. 3 pick in the 2025 NFL Draft, but his rookie season was a rocky one. He finished with just four sacks and was benched twice for off-field issues. Carter set a goal of winning Defensive Player of the Year in his second season. But he entered Sunday with just two sacks through nine games and had gone four straight games without one, though he has faced more double-teams with Pro Bowl linebacker Brian Burns out since Week 3 with a torn ACL. Giants head coach John Harbaugh insisted last week that the production would come. “I believe the sacks will come. He’s a disruptive guy. I promise you they’re accounting for him, and the sacks are just going to come,” Harbaugh said, via The Associated Press . Carter was even more confident. After tweeting that he would show everyone on Sunday, he told NJ.com’s Darryl Slater what he planned to prove against the Jaguars. “I’m just going to show the world why I’m going to be the greatest ever. And that’s it. Simple as that,” Carter said. ‘I’m the Best in the World’ Carter backed it up in a big way on Sunday, putting pressure on Lawrence all afternoon as the Giants built a 20-6 halftime lead and held on for the win. The Giants improved to 6-3-1 and kept their lead in the NFC East, despite being on their third starting quarterback of the season in J.J. McCarthy. After the game, Carter did not hold back when asked about the win. “As a defense, we showed what we really about. And for me, I’m the best in the world,” Carter said, via NFL on CBS . He doubled down in the locker room when he was reminded that he promised to show why he would be the greatest ever. “I’m the best in the world,” Carter said, via the Giants . item.title: Jets & Chargers combine for NFL history not seen in over 50 years
item.description: The New York Jets and Los Angeles Chargers made NFL history on Sunday, producing a statistical oddity that had not been seen in more than five decades during their Week 11 matchup. item.description: FIFA announced Monday that the USA will co-host the 2031 Women's World Cup with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica, while the UK will host in 2035 (OZAN KOSE) FIFA on Monday confirmed that a joint bid led by the United States will host the expanded, 48-team Women's World Cup in 2031, while the United Kingdom will host the following edition in 2035. The winning bids were waved through by acclamation after FIFA president Gianni Infantino confirmed the USA in partnership with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica was the "sole candidacy" to host in 2031, when the tournament will feature 48 teams for the first time. The joint English, Scottish, Northern Irish and Welsh bid was also the only candidacy for 2035. Infantino had already revealed last year that the respective bids for 2031 and 2035 were unchallenged and therefore set to be awarded the tournaments, with both being officially rubber-stamped at a virtual gathering of FIFA's member associations. "As of 2031 there will be 48 teams and four hosts," said Infantino. "This is an incredible growth in just a few years." The next Women's World Cup will take place next year in Brazil, running from June 24 to July 25. It will feature 32 teams, with the final at the Maracana Stadium in Rio de Janeiro. Spain go into that tournament as the holders after winning the last Women's World Cup held in Australia and New Zealand in 2023, when they defeated current European champions England in the final. The US co-hosted this year's men's World Cup, with the majority of matches being played on American soil, including the final at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey which was won by Spain. That was the first men's edition featuring 48 teams. The USA has hosted the Women's World Cup twice before, in 1999 and 2003, and is also the most successful nation in the tournament's history, having lifted the trophy four times. - 'Landmark moment' - US Soccer reacted to the announcement by saying the awarding of the 2031 tournament gave the country the chance to "build on the momentum" of this year's World Cup as well as the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. The United States are the reigning Olympic women's football champions. No senior men's or women's World Cup has been played in the UK since England hosted and won the men's edition in 1966. A joint statement by the four UK national associations described the announcement as "a landmark moment". It is not yet known which cities will host matches at the respective tournaments, but most matches in 2031 are likely to take place in the United States while England can expect to have the lion's share of venues in 2035. item.title: Bucks to continue to push league for NBA All-Star game in Milwaukee
item.description: Despite losing the 2028 NBA All-Star Game to Miami, the Milwaukee Bucks will continue pushing NBA officials for the event. The club believes Milwaukee has everything the NBA needs to host such an event. “We’re going to constantly bring it up with the league,” said Bucks president Josh Glessing. “The opportunity to showcase Milwaukee via the All-Star Game is so important. The economic impact and activity it creates in a region is so powerful." Glessing admits the pitch for Milwaukee does have some "challenges." “What we know is there’s a minimum threshold of hotel rooms and we have work to do there,” Glessing said adding the team has helped build two new hotels in The Trade and AC Hotel by Marriot which is currently under construction. The NBA requires the host city of the All-Star Game to have 7,250 hotel rooms. According to Visit Milwaukee there are 190 hotel properties in the area equaling about 20,000 rooms. It's unclear how many four and five-star hotels are required for the host city. Visit Milwaukee has not talked to the NBA about Milwaukee hosting the all-star game but is supportive of a bid. More: Milwaukee Bucks approach new challenge: getting fans engaged, in seats Glessing is not a stranger to All-Star Games. When he was interim-president of business operations for the Columbus Crew, the organization hosted the MLS All-Star Game in 2024. Glessing said for the team, the All-Star Game is a "money loser" but an event like that has broader economic potential for a city. “It’s a tremendous amount of work and the local teams put so much effort into it, but for the teams it is not a boon in any stretch,” Glessing said. “But for the local economy its so powerful, it’s so impactful to all of the people and activity and dollars that are spent locally. It’s not just a one-day event, it’s a weeklong event. So, the ability to highlight the city is huge.” This article originally appeared on Milwaukee Journal Sentinel: Bucks to continue to push league for NBA All-Star game in Milwaukee

item.title: Do Cowboys Fans Have Playoff Hope During Thanksgiving Week?
item.description: turkey dak jerry Somebody once said, “Hope is not a plan.” But what if “hope” is just about all you have left to cling to? The Dallas Cowboys crushed the lowly Tennessee Titans, 51-30, Sunday at AT&T Stadium and in doing so fueled optimism inside the locker room. “It gives me hope that we can do some of the things that we want to do,” said owner Jerry Jones (who was technically standing outside the locker room, but you get the point). “We want to get better defensively, and we want to execute like that offensively. “That thing went exactly like it was mapped out to go.” That rings true. Dak Prescott had a historic day, going 28-of-33 for 325 yards and four TDs, while the offense scored TDs on its first six possessions. And on defense? Oh, they gave up yards and they gave up points, but Quinnen Williams led the charge on a five-sack day, capping a week in which young defensive coordinator Christian Parker was demoted , with Mike Pettine now the play-caller. But later in the day came the problem. The Cowboys may have “mapped out” a win, and they can do the same thing as it regards a pursuit of the NFC East title and a playoff berth. But once Jerry and the ’Boys got home to do some scoreboard-watching? They discovered that the Giants pulled off a 23-18 upset over the Jacksonville Jaguars, moving New York to 6-3-1 … meaning that even though Dallas is 5-6, no ground was actually gained. Can Cowboys Nation allow itself to get excited about topping the one-win Titans? Hey, Dallas has lost home games to the Bucs and the Cardinals, so you take the win. Can Dallas fans count on a Thanksgiving win over the visiting (and semi-tanking) Philadelphia Eagles on Thursday? Hey, Dallas is an 8.5-point favorite , so that’s a start. But in the end, does it add up to playoff “hope” for Dallas? Cowboys Nation, you will have to make up your own mind on that one.

item.title: Eagles star Joe Milton reveals the secret trick he uses every time just before he throws a deep pass
item.description: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles picked up a 19-16 upset win over the Pittsburgh Steelers, and Joe Milton played his part. The 26-year-old quarterback was only signed in October this year, following Jalen Hurts’ injury, and he has now started back-to-back games. Against the Steelers, Milton showed off his passing ability, and he revealed the trick he uses to program his mind not to overthrow. Joe Milton says his daughter’s name before every deep pass Milton played a turnover-free, game-manager role in his second start for the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday. The quarterback seemed to develop a good partnership with DeVonta Smith, targeting him 12 times out of his 21 pass attempts. One of his pass attempts flew over the wide receiver’s head, much to his surprise. “I didn’t think I could get overthrown. And he did it,” Smith said. After the game, Milton was asked how he decides when to go hard and when not to when he’s in the middle. The quarterback revealed that his secret trick involves using his daughter’s name. He said, as per NBCS Philly: “Just showing a little love. In throws like that, I usually say my daughter’s name. It helps me relax. I didn’t that time (overthrown pass to Smith), obviously. “Right before I throw the ball, just get a quick little ‘Maleia’, just so I can relax a little bit. Basically, it kind of tells myself and my mind that I’m throwing the ball to her, so it can’t be as hard. “So, show a little love.” Sunday was the first time Smith and Milton played together for the Philadelphia Eagles, and early signs are definitely positive. The quarterback finished the game with 141 passing yards while completing 11 of his 21 passes, boasting a 73.7 passer rating. He also added seven rushing yards on five carries and took three sacks. Milton hasn’t thrown a touchdown pass for the Eagles yet, but he is in line to start against the Dallas Cowboys next, who are his former team. We’re sure he would love to break his duck then. (Photo by Nathanial George/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Mondays are objectively terrible for many working folks, but having to gather among other humans after a fourth Ohio State loss on the season is starting to feel like a special kind of torture. The last time the Buckeyes lost so many times in a season, this column had never been published before, so I’m in uncharted territory having to pick through the smoldering rubbish heap of yet another L, but here we are… Here is a partial list of what turned Midwestern nice into a Midwestern nightmare on Saturday. Disorganization starts at the top There are a lot of things going wrong with the Buckeyes these days, including a lot of preventable things that continue to pile up. It started early, with Ryan Day getting flagged for sideline interference on Jeremiah Smith’s first touchdown. The 15-yard penalty on the ensuing kickoff gave Nebraska starting position at its 37-yard line, helping the Huskers quickly tie the game. I don’t know if the Buckeyes were having communication issues, but the number of times the play clock ran way down and the use of timeouts to combat that was weird. Using a timeout on the first possession of the third quarter was costly, and using one to avoid a delay-of-game infraction when it was already third-and-a-mile seemed unnecessary (and the opposite of the earlier strategy of taking the five yards in the same situation). Late in the game, that mattered, as Ohio State was again far too deliberate while chasing a two-score game and did not have sufficient remaining timeouts to get the ball back at the end after pulling back within three points. If you’re going to expect the players to execute, the coaching staff has to stop putting them in difficult spots. Third downs matter Ohio State’s alarming third-down defensive (in)efficiency continues to be alarming. Nebraska went 10-for-16 on third downs, and on two of the six that the Buckeyes stopped, the Cornhuskers converted on fourth down (2/2). So, out of the 16 times Ohio State forced the hosts into a third-down situation, Nebraska picked up a first down on 12 of those times. Matt Patricia’s defense has fallen to 109th nationally in third-down efficiency. Only Michigan State, Rutgers, and Purdue are worse on third down in the Big Ten. item.title: Josh Allen Spots Rookie Jacob Rodriguez And Shows Massive Respect
item.description: Credit: Amber Searls-Imagn Images Josh Allen stayed on the field after the Bills beat the Dolphins 26-9 on Sunday just to find rookie linebacker Jacob Rodriguez. The Bills quarterback hunted down the Miami defender, hugged him, and exchanged quick words before heading to the locker room. This moment stood out because Allen usually leaves right after his postgame chat with the media. The game on Sunday, Nov. 22, was a tough night for Allen statistically, even though his team won big. He threw for 304 yards and a touchdown but also tossed two interceptions. Miami’s defense held him to a quarterback rating under 70 and sacked him three times. Rodriguez was a major part of that pressure, finishing with a team-high 13 tackles and one interception. Allen didn’t just leave it at a quick nod. He waited for the rookie to finish his own media obligations. Most veterans do not wait that long for a rookie from a rival team, especially one who just made their life hard. Phin Phanatic noted that Allen’s search showed real respect for the young player’s performance. The Rookie Who Stole the Show Rodriguez made his mark early in the game. He picked off Allen near the end of the first half. It was the second interception of the season for the rookie. Virginia’s Rodriguez began his collegiate tenure as an offensive role/QB after in 2021 then being selected as an All-American linebacker from Texas Tech – 43rd overall in the 2026 class. That shared background might be why Allen wanted to talk to him so badly. Heavy.com reported that fans on social media praised the gesture immediately. One user called it a “Top 10 football respect moment.” Even some Miami fans admitted they found it hard to hate Allen after seeing this. One fan wrote, “As a Dolphins [fan]… it’s hard not to like Josh Allen. He’s a good guy.” A Rare Quiet Game for Allen While the hug got the headlines, the game itself had a strange stat line for the Bills star. Andrew Siciliano pointed out that Allen did not have a single rushing attempt during the entire game. This was the first time in his nine-year NFL career that he played a full game without trying to run the ball. The Bills chose not to let Allen run on a goal-line sneak. James Cook received the handoff instead, scoring a one-yard touchdown. Allen admitted he was not happy with his own play despite the win. He said, “You got to play your best and tonight I don’t feel like I did.” He also noted that he had two bad decisions, one being a tipped pass. “So, got a lot to clean up,” Allen said in his postgame press conference. He added, “It’s very much a luxury to sit here, be 9-1 and be a little ticked off about how you played.” Now the Bills face a short week. They will host the Kansas City Chiefs on Thursday, Nov. 26. The next game for the Dolphins is Sunday, Nov. 29, against the New York Jets.

By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office.
